tob-10020: Written under the pen name Yogi Ramacharaka, William Walker Atkinson offers a mystical reading of the life and teachings of Jesus. He blends Christian doctrine with Eastern ideas about inner spiritual development, presenting Christ as a great spiritual teacher rather than only a figure of church dogma. The book was popular in the early 1900s among readers of New Thought, a movement that stressed the power of the mind.
tob-10220: Bertrand Russell wrote this short book in 1912 to show ordinary readers what philosophy is actually for. He walks through questions like whether we can trust our senses, what makes a belief true, and whether the physical world is real — and shows why asking them matters even when no final answer exists. Clear and free of jargon, it has introduced generations of students to philosophical thinking.
tob-10920: Albert Pike’s massive 1871 work expounds the philosophy behind the thirty-two degrees of Scottish Rite Freemasonry. Drawing on ancient religions, Kabbalah, and Hermetic wisdom, he interprets each degree’s symbols as lessons in morality and self-mastery. Revered by Masons and quoted by conspiracy theorists alike, it is the most famous Masonic book ever written.
tob-4020: John Locke’s Essay asks one plain question with huge fallout: where do our ideas come from? His answer — from experience, not from inborn truths — swept away old certainties and made him the thinker of the Enlightenment. This first volume covers Books 1 and 2, knocking down inborn ideas and touring the senses.
tob-0020: The Infancy Gospel of Thomas spins wild tales of Jesus as a boy — striking playmates dead and raising them, shaping sparrows of clay that fly off alive. First Christians doted on these stories, though the church never took the book in. The text shows how the faithful pictured the holy child’s hidden years.
tob-0120: The Protocols is a black forgery — a faked plot for Jewish world-rule, cooked up by the Tsar’s secret police about 1903. Though shown false again and again, it fed Jew-hating bloodshed for a hundred years. This entry keeps it as a record of hate, not as truth.
tob-4120: John Parker’s 1897 Englishing gives the Areopagite’s works — the veiled writer whose Angel-ranks and God-names molded medieval holy thought. His sight of God past all names swayed a thousand years of God-lore. The volume made the Areopagite speak English.
cia-0000098720: A July 1981 report on the Soviet Union sharing anti-submarine weapons and know-how with its Warsaw Pact allies in Eastern Europe. cia-0000107420: A September 1984 report on trends in South Africa's nuclear security policies and programs. The document tracks how American intelligence assessed the bomb program of an apartheid state — a uniquely dangerous combination.

plos-pone-0003420: Geneticists charted the social network of tiny RNAs in this 2008 study. plos-pone-0003520: Yeast geneticists found a nutrient sensor deciding cells' fate in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003620: Psychiatric geneticists Enoch, Shen, and Ducci linked brain waves, drinking, and worry to one gene system in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003720: In 2008, Schlee, Weisz, and Bertrand mapped the ringing-ear brain. plos-pone-0003820: In 2008, a team released NMRDyn, software for watching proteins pair up. The program reads NMR relaxation data to study how proteins associate and move at the atomic scale. The tool helps biophysicists measure the dynamics of protein partnerships that underlie cell processes.

plos-pone-0004120: In 2009, Heslop, Miller, and Hill found zip code outliving good medicine. Poorer neighbourhoods predicted more non-cardiovascular deaths among cardiac patients in Canada. Canada's universal care did not erase the steep gradient. The stark result pins health gaps on social ground.
plos-pone-0004220: In 2009, Aabye, Ravn, and PrayGod tested a TB test under HIV's shadow. HIV infection and low CD4 counts weakened interferon gamma release assay performance. The TB blood test lost accuracy in co-infected patients. The finding tunes TB screening in HIV zones.
plos-pone-0004320: In 2009, Yonehara, Ishikane, and Sakuta mapped motion detectors in the eye. Direction-selective retinal ganglion cells and their projections were charted. plos-pone-0358120: Diabetes and anemia often travel together — and the combination is dangerous. plos-pone-0357020: The tear film’s lipid layer keeps eyes moist — and its thickness varies more than assumed. plos-pone-0355720: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria exhausts patients — crushing fatigue is its hallmark. plos-pone-0348820: College athletes with hip and pelvis problems need fast, field-ready triage. plos-pone-0357920: Pharmacy-led PrEP could massively expand HIV prevention — if the service model is right. plos-pone-0356920: Sámi and non-Sámi teenagers in Arctic Norway navigate the internet’s risks differently. plos-pone-0354920: Preparing for bird flu means rehearsing the outbreak before it happens. plos-pone-0348720: Holding community healthcare accountable in Bangladesh’s marginalized communities requires trustworthy measurement. plos-pone-0355020: Adults with sickle cell disease face wrenching decisions about having children. plos-pone-0356820: Fatty liver disease ages the liver differently than healthy aging does. plos-pone-0356720: Folate deficiency in early pregnancy causes devastating neural tube defects — and Tigray, Ethiopia is a high-risk region. plos-pone-0348920: Deworming schoolchildren for schistosomiasis only works if the program is actually delivered as designed. plos-pone-0356620: When dangerous food hits American shelves, recalls follow — but the patterns were unmapped. plos-pone-0355620: Colorectal cancer patients with ostomies depend on their caregivers’ skills — measurably. plos-pone-0355520: This entry is a correction notice, not a research finding. It amends the paper on myeloid-derived suppressor cells contributing to malignant progression of oral squamous cell carcinoma. Readers should consult the corrected version for the accurate record.
europmc-pmc2791220: Why do some people keep HIV in check without drugs? This 2009 genetics paper looks for common DNA differences linked to how well humans control HIV-1 infection. The researchers scanned thousands of genomes for variants tied to lower virus levels and slower disease progress. Their map of genetic factors opened new leads for therapies and vaccines.
europmc-pmc2799520: Telling medicinal plants apart by looks alone is hard, so this 2010 paper proposes a DNA shortcut. The authors validate a short stretch of DNA called ITS2 as a barcode for identifying medicinal plant species. They test it across many species and show it tells them apart reliably. europmc-pmc2832020: Diabetic wounds heal slowly, and this 2010 paper finds faulty macrophages are part of the reason. The work points to immune repair as a target for diabetic wound therapies.
europmc-pmc2841820: Knee osteoarthritis may announce itself in the blood years before X-rays show damage. europmc-pmc2856220: Broken bones in kids follow patterns, and this 2010 paper charts them. The authors study the epidemiology of fractures in children and teens, mapping which breaks hit which ages. europmc-pmc2877420: Melioidosis, a tropical disease caught from soil germs, was rising in Northeast Thailand. europmc-pmc2901520: The hunger hormone ghrelin does more than signal empty stomachs. This 2010 rodent study shows ghrelin pushes extra intake of tasty, rewarding food. europmc-pmc2912920: Pilot studies get lip service but little clarity. This 2010 review asks what a pilot or feasibility study truly is, surveying current practice and journal rules. The authors find confusion reigns across fields. Their paper pushed journals to demand real pilot standards.
europmc-pmc2919420: Protein clumps may be part of normal aging, not just disease. This 2010 worm study finds widespread protein aggregation as an inherent part of aging in C. elegans. europmc-pmc2919520: Reading population history from DNA takes the right software. europmc-pmc2949620: Evolutionary clocks tick at different rates, and this 2010 paper models the variation. The authors introduce Bayesian random local clocks for dating evolutionary events. europmc-pmc2954820: Losing one gene copy can sicken, and this 2010 paper predicts when. The authors characterize and predict haploinsufficiency across the human genome. Their model flags vulnerable genes. Their work aids interpreting genetic tests. Doctors use such scores to judge rare variants.

europmc-pmc6511120: Schizophrenia looks like a wiring problem in the brain, but no one knew how that faulty wiring connects to the genes behind it. The two lined up, suggesting the genes help shape the very brain networks that go wrong in psychosis.
europmc-pmc6724220: Lung cancer kills more Americans than any other cancer - but the global picture varies wildly. The disparities point to where prevention can save the most lives.
europmc-pmc6745820: Finding distant protein relatives is detective work - and HH-suite3 is a faster magnifying glass. The software suite detects remote homology and annotates proteins deeply, using profile hidden Markov models. The upgrade speeds the searches biologists run daily.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-20: Tied to base closings, this 2007 GAO report asks what would break if the military's famed pathology lab shut down, moved, or went private. gao-gaoreports-gao-07-920: The roads were full in 2007 — GAO's report says smarter use could squeeze more from the pavement we had. The findings lay out strategies for making existing highways hum. The report's contrarian bet: the cheapest new lane is the one you never have to build.
